children: Chicago soybean and corn futures extended losses on Wednesday as funds liquidated long positions and US farmers stepped up harvesting of large crops.
The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
fell 0.02% to $12.48 a bushel by 0140 GMT, hovering near its lowest in eight weeks. CBOT corn

Favourable harvest weather forecast across the Midwest through at least the end of the week added pressure, as farmers gathered what is expected to be a record-large US soybean crop and the second-largest corn crop on record.
Harvest pressure outweighed support from renewed Chinese demand as the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) confirmed more purchases by the world's top soy importer.
Heavy bullish positioning in the soy complex leaves limited room for further gains and increases the risk of a sharp correction, BMI, a Fitch Solutions research unit, said in a note.
"The ongoing US harvest will replenish near-term supplies, while the advancement of Brazil's season will shift attention towards a 185 million ton crop in 2026/27," it said.

In Brazil, farmers had planted 26% of the projected area of their 2026/27 soybean crop as of last Thursday, agribusiness consultancy AgRural said on Monday, up from 15% a week earlier and above the 24% registered a year ago.

US farmers have harvested 64% of the soybean crop and 44% of the corn crop, according to the USDA's weekly crop progress report released on Monday. Both figures were below trade expectations. Winter wheat planting was 63% complete, also below analysts' expectations of 65%.
fell 0.31% to $6.41-1/4 a bushel, hitting a more-than-two-month low.

"US wheat futures continued to ease, as drier conditions in the US are expected to accelerate winter wheat planting and the pressure continues from robust global stocks,"  Bendigo Bank Agribusiness said in a note.
Wheat traders also continued to assess disruptions to Black Sea grain exports caused by Russia's war in Ukraine.
Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn, soybeans and wheat on Tuesday, traders said. (CBOT/FUNDS)
